checks.label: Default Encryption Password Check
checks.description: Safe ONLY when '0'. '1' means encryption uses default password, which is insecure. Strict anchoring avoids matching numbers inside longer strings.
checks.remediation: Set a strong user-chosen encryption password via Settings > Security. Avoid leaving the default password in place.

checks.label: Encryption Completion Status
checks.description: Full Disk Encryption is complete only if output is exactly '1'. A strict equality match ensures no accidental pattern hits.
checks.remediation: If encryption is incomplete, reboot and allow it to finish. If it fails, re-initiate encryption from recovery mode.

checks.label: Data Partition Encryption Check
checks.description: Safe ONLY if /data is mounted on a 'dm-*' device, which indicates encryption. Raw eMMC partitions ('mmcblk0pXX') mean unencrypted storage. This match is stable because dm- devices cannot appear in plain, unencrypted mounts.
checks.remediation: Enable device encryption so /data is mounted via dm-crypt. Back up data first, then encrypt from Settings or recovery.

checks.label: FBE FUSE Layer Status
checks.description: File-Based Encryption is active only if output is exactly 'true'. Anchors prevent accidental matches of longer boolean strings.
checks.remediation: Enable file-based encryption (FBE) in device settings or reflash with an FBE-enabled firmware image.

checks.label: Service-Based Encryption Check
checks.description: Encryption is typically active when the response contains '00000001'. Because binder output is structured, this specific pattern is reliable with minimal false-positive risk.
checks.remediation: Enable device encryption via Settings > Security. If the mount service reports inactive, reboot and retry.

checks.label: SD Card Encryption
checks.description: Safe ONLY when output is exactly '1'. Strict match prevents accidental detection from logs or metadata containing '1'.
checks.remediation: Encrypt the SD card via Settings > Security > Encrypt SD card. Remove sensitive data from unencrypted cards.

checks.label: SD Card Mount Check
checks.description: Safe if SD card is mounted via dm-crypt or FUSE. Pattern is strict enough to avoid accidental substring matches on unrelated mount entries.
checks.remediation: Encrypt the SD card so it mounts through dm-crypt or FUSE. Reformat and re-encrypt if mounted as plain storage.

checks.label: Hardware Keystore
checks.remediation: Use a device with a hardware-backed keystore (TEE/SE). Avoid storing sensitive keys in software-only keystores.

checks.label: Crypto FS State
checks.remediation: If decryption is stalled, reboot the device. Ensure a valid encryption password is set to allow proper unlock.

checks.label: StrongBox Support
checks.remediation: Use a device with StrongBox support for highest key protection. Migrate critical keys to hardware-backed storage.

checks.label: Hardcoded Passwords in Config
checks.description: Config files containing password-related keywords (keyword detection - verify manually whether actual credentials are present)
checks.remediation: Remove hardcoded passwords from config files. Use a secrets manager or environment variables instead.

checks.label: API Keys in Files
checks.description: Files containing API key-related keywords (keyword detection - verify manually whether actual secrets are present)
checks.remediation: Remove API keys from files. Store them in Android Keystore or a secure secrets management solution.

checks.label: Private Keys Exposed
checks.description: Private key files found - should be protected
checks.remediation: Delete unnecessary private key files. Move required keys to hardware-backed storage with strict permissions.

checks.label: SSH Keys on Device
checks.description: SSH keys found - review if needed
checks.remediation: Remove SSH keys that are not required. Restrict file permissions to owner-only (chmod 600) for any that remain.

checks.label: Default Credential Files
checks.description: Credential files in system - check permissions
checks.remediation: Remove default credential files from /system and /vendor. Use Android Keystore for credential management.

checks.label: Hardcoded URLs with Credentials
checks.remediation: Replace embedded credentials in URLs with token-based auth or secure credential storage.

checks.label: Database Files with Potential Secrets
checks.description: Database files - may contain sensitive data
checks.remediation: Audit database files for sensitive data. Encrypt databases using SQLCipher or restrict access with strict permissions.

checks.label: KeyMint HAL Present
checks.description: KeyMint HAL (Android 12+) provides stronger key attestation and hardware-backed cryptography than legacy Keymaster. Absence may indicate an older or less-secure keystore implementation.
checks.remediation: Update to Android 12+ firmware with KeyMint HAL support. Avoid relying on legacy Keymaster for key attestation.
